title: Daytime drop-in funding and intimate partner violence epidemic
subtitle: Advisory committee framework, council expense policy, committee appointments and awards for accessibility and young dancers
overview: Council agreed to extend the pilot daytime drop-in program with Royal City Mission for January to March 2024, offering service six days a week. The City will pay up to $21,322 per month, for a total of $63,966, from the Tax Rate Operating Contingency Reserve {{vote:m10}}. It was described as a temporary measure for this winter while a county housing symposium considers longer-term funding. A second proposal in the staff report was held back until after that symposium.

Council declared intimate partner violence and violence against women an epidemic {{vote:m11}}. It asked the province to do the same and urged other governments to act on the Renfrew County inquest recommendations. Staff will look at naming the issue as a priority in the Community Plan, and the Police Services Board was asked for a report.

Council also approved a governance framework for advisory committees, with an amendment, and paused most new recruitment until late 2024 {{vote:m7}}. It adopted an updated Mayor and Council expense and education policy {{vote:m4}} and made appointments to the Committee of Adjustment and The Elliott board {{vote:m2}}. The meeting also recognized accessibility award recipients and young Guelph dancers.

decisions.detail: Staff were directed to extend the Royal City Mission pilot from January 1 to March 31, 2024, six days a week, at up to $21,322 per month ($63,966 total) from the Tax Rate Operating Contingency Reserve.
Council received the staff report on daytime drop-in services for information.

Council declared intimate partner violence an epidemic, asked the province to do likewise, urged action on the inquest recommendations, and directed staff to consider the issue for the Community Plan and Community Safety and Wellbeing Plan.
Council approved the framework as amended, directed staff to apply it to existing committees and report back in Q4 2024, and paused most recruitment until then.

decisions.item: Mayor and Council expense and education policy
decisions.detail: Council approved the updated policy and repealed the Policy on Councillor Attendance at Municipal Events.
Council appointed one person to the Committee of Adjustment and made three appointments or reappointments to The Elliott Community Board of Trustees.

debate: Delegates urged Council to fund the drop-in service, describing it as a place of community and warmth for vulnerable people, including refugees and people facing eviction, and said it eases pressure on health, police and library services.

Royal City Mission representatives said the earlier agreement funded four hours but required 12 hours of opening. They said guaranteeing 12 hours needed guaranteed funding, as demand and staffing costs had risen while donations were flat.

Councillors asked for financial detail such as budget breakdowns, audited statements and whether city money paid for capital improvements. Staff of the mission said audited statements were available and city money had not gone to capital work.

One councillor noted that daytime shelter was not historically a municipal responsibility and called the extension a stopgap until the county's winter housing symposium. Another raised the pressure on the City's own budget the next day.

In support of the epidemic declaration, a Women in Crisis delegate argued that an epidemic need not be contagious and that the acceptable number of cases is zero. The mover cited the inquest recommendations and more than 70 other municipalities.
